relationships.subject: lambda-carrageenan
relationships.evidence_quote: On the other hand, intraprostatic injection of 3% λ-carrageenan led to the inflammation of the prostate (CP/CPPS group, Figures 3(b)–3(d)).

relationships.subject: chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome
relationships.evidence_quote: Scrotal pain thresholds in CP/CPPS rats were highly significantly reduced (p < 0.001) compared to the thresholds in sham rats on the 2nd, 3rd, and 7th day upon intraprostatic injection (Figure 2).

relationships.subject: chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome
relationships.evidence_quote: Ethological tests (open field, elevated plus maze, and light/dark tests) revealed significantly increased anxiety-like behavior in rats with CP/CPPS comparing to their sham-operated mates starting from day 3, and there were significant intercorrelations among parameters of these tests.

relationships.subject: chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome
relationships.evidence_quote: Results of biochemical analyses showed a statistically significant increase of the MDA level in the hippocampus (p < 0.01), thalamus (p < 0.001), and cortex (p < 0.001) of CP/CPPS animals compared with sham mates (Figure 7(a)).

relationships.subject: chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome
relationships.evidence_quote: SOD activity has been uniformly decreased in the hippocampus (p < 0.001), thalamus (p < 0.01), and cerebral cortex (p < 0.001) in the CP/CPPS group compared to the activity of this enzyme in corresponding structures isolated from the sham group (Figure 7(c)).

relationships.subject: chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome
relationships.evidence_quote: Serum corticosterone level analysis showed a significant increase in corticosterone level in serum of CP/CPPS animals, compared to the sham group (p < 0.05, Figure 8).

relationships.subject: chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome
relationships.evidence_quote: As shown in Figure 9(c), CP/CPPS animals had significantly less PV+ interneurons in CA1, CA2/3, and DG regions of the hippocampus, compared to sham animals (p < 0.01).

relationships.subject: chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome
relationships.evidence_quote: CP/CPPS animals showed a significantly lower thiol group content in all brain structures than sham animals, i.e., hippocampus (p < 0.001), thalamus (p < 0.001), and cortex (p < 0.001; Figure 7(d)).

relationships.subject: brain oxidative stress
relationships.evidence_quote: Therefore, the potential mechanisms of observed behavioral alterations in CP/CPPS rats could be the result of an interplay between increased brain oxidative stress, elevated serum corticosterone level, and loss of hippocampal PV+ interneurons.

relationships.subject: hippocampal parvalbumin-positive interneurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Simple regression analysis indicated that the number of PV+ interneurons in CA2/3 was positively correlated with time CP/CPPS animals spent in the open arms of the EPM (r = 0.835, p < 0.05) and time in the light compartment of the L/D test (r = 0.969, p < 0.001).

key_findings: Intraprostatic lambda-carrageenan produced prostatitis and scrotal allodynia in rats, accompanied by significantly increased anxiety-like behavior from day 3 across open field, elevated plus maze and light/dark tests.

The anxiety correlated with raised brain MDA (hippocampus and cortex), reduced SOD and thiol content, elevated serum corticosterone and fewer hippocampal parvalbumin-positive interneurons in CA1, CA2/3 and dentate gyrus.
